# Item 113 — the reviewed German catalogue

This is the complete German catalogue as it stands in
`src/i18n/messages.de.ts` **after human linguistic review**, regenerated
from that catalogue rather than maintained by hand. Every row carries the
reviewer's decision, and the 37 entries they annotated carry the note
verbatim — several of those notes asked for coordinated English-source
corrections, which stage 6b carries out.

## Summary

|                                        |         |
| -------------------------------------- | ------- |
| Total keys                             | **739** |
| Plain entries                          | 719     |
| Plural entries (`one` / `other`)       | 18      |
| Rich entries (React nodes substituted) | 2       |
| Accepted unchanged                     | 417     |
| Replaced during review                 | 322     |
| Carrying a reviewer note               | 37      |
| Deliberately identical to English      | 44      |

Machine-checked and passing: key parity, entry-shape parity,
placeholder-name parity per plural category, every message rendered with
English-derived parameters leaving no unsubstituted brace, German plural
selection, informal address, German quotation marks, and no hard-coded
decimal separator. **None of that ever said the German was _right_** — the
human review did, and this document is its record.

## How to read a row

`Kind` is `plain`, `plural` or `rich`. A plural row shows `one` and
`other` on separate lines. `{name}` is a placeholder substituted at
runtime; its name is identical in both languages, but its **position may
differ**, which is deliberate. `Where` names the module that renders it.

`Decision` is the reviewer's: **accepted** kept the drafted German,
**replaced** substituted their own wording.

⚠ marks wording where a mistranslation would matter most: a destructive
or irreversible action, a safety or accuracy qualification, or a sentence
that must not imply turn-by-turn navigation, background tracking, offline
map storage or guaranteed recovery.

| `status.fetchFailureDetail`                         | plain | replaced | Browsers may report a generic fetch failure instead of the real HTTP status (for example 502) when the provider's error response is missing CORS headers — an entry reading "Fetch promise rejected before an HTTP response was exposed" can mean a provider outage, a missing CORS header, a DNS or TLS failure, or a local network restriction, and cannot be told apart from this information alone. | Browser zeigen möglicherweise einen allgemeinen Netzwerkfehler statt des tatsächlichen HTTP-Statuscodes an, wenn in der Fehlerantwort des Anbieters die erforderlichen CORS-Header fehlen. Der Eintrag „Die Netzwerkanfrage schlug fehl, bevor der Browser eine HTTP-Antwort bereitstellte“ kann daher auf eine Störung beim Anbieter, fehlende CORS-Header, einen DNS- oder TLS-Fehler oder eine lokale Netzwerkbeschränkung zurückgehen. Allein anhand dieses Eintrags lassen sich diese Ursachen nicht unterscheiden. | —                                    | `ui/diagnostics/DiagnosticsScreen.tsx`   | ⚠ Replace the overloaded source sentence with the revised three-sentence copy in both catalogues. German: Browser zeigen möglicherweise einen allgemeinen Netzwerkfehler statt des tatsächlichen HTTP-Statuscodes an, wenn in der Fehlerantwort des Anbieters die erforderlichen CORS-Header fehlen. Der Eintrag „Die Netzwerkanfrage schlug fehl, bevor der Browser eine HTTP-Antwort bereitstellte“ kann daher auf eine Störung beim Anbieter, fehlende CORS-Header, einen DNS- oder TLS-Fehler oder eine lokale Netzwerkbeschränkung zurückgehen. Allein anhand dieses Eintrags lassen sich diese Ursachen nicht unterscheiden. English: Browsers may report a generic network failure instead of the actual HTTP status code, such as 502, when the provider’s error response lacks the required CORS headers. An entry reading “The network request failed before the browser exposed an HTTP response” may therefore indicate a provider outage, missing CORS headers, a DNS or TLS failure, or a local network restriction. This information alone cannot distinguish between those causes. The quoted log entry must come from routingLog.noResponseExposed, not be duplicated inside status.fetchFailureDetail. Add a named {entry} placeholder to status.fetchFailureDetail and supply it with the localised value of routingLog.noResponseExposed. Use these coordinated log-entry translations: English: The network request failed before the browser exposed an HTTP response German: Die Netzwerkanfrage schlug fehl, bevor der Browser eine HTTP-Antwort bereitstellte Preserve the diagnostic distinction: the browser exposed no HTTP response to the application, but this does not prove that the provider sent no response. these stops being identical without its justification being removed, or
if a new identical entry appears without one.

### Content that never enters the catalogue at all

Unchanged from the stage 5 residual-copy audit, and unchanged by German:

- **user content** — route names, tags, and anything typed by the rider;
- **provider and imported text** — openrouteservice manoeuvre
  instructions and road names, and raw GPX content. A route may hold
  English manoeuvres from an earlier calculation, German ones from a
  later one, and imported ones in any language at once. **Changing the
  interface language translates nothing that is already stored and
  recalculates nothing**; no message in this catalogue claims otherwise;
- **machine tokens** — HTTP statuses, exception names such as
  `TypeError`, provider categories, transport reason codes, schema keys,
  URLs, CSS classes, `data-testid` values and internal screen keys;
- **product and organisation names** — `ACN`, `GPX`, `OpenRouteService`,
  `HeiGIT`, `OpenStreetMap`, `OpenFreeMap`;
- **the copied diagnostic report**, which stays entirely English under
  approved decision R4. It reads its one shared sentence through the
  English translator explicitly, so it is English _by construction_. The
  German Status interface around it is translated, and stage 6b should
  add one German sentence saying the report itself is English so it can
  be shared for support — **that sentence is not yet written**, because
  it needs a new key and therefore a new English entry too.

Allein anhand dieses Eintrags lassen sich diese Ursachen nicht unterscheiden. English: Browsers may report a generic network failure instead of the actual HTTP status code, such as 502, when the provider’s error response lacks the required CORS headers. An entry reading “The network request failed before the browser exposed an HTTP response” may therefore indicate a provider outage, missing CORS headers, a DNS or TLS failure, or a local network restriction. This information alone cannot distinguish between those causes. The quoted log entry must come from routingLog.noResponseExposed, not be duplicated inside status.fetchFailureDetail. Add a named {entry} placeholder to status.fetchFailureDetail and supply it with the localised value of routingLog.noResponseExposed. Use these coordinated log-entry translations: English: The network request failed before the browser exposed an HTTP response German: Die Netzwerkanfrage schlug fehl, bevor der Browser eine HTTP-Antwort bereitstellte Preserve the diagnostic distinction: the browser exposed no HTTP response to the application, but this does not prove that the provider sent no response. Add focused tests showing that the disclosure interpolates the exact log wording in both languages, so the two surfaces cannot drift independently. |

## What stage 6b carries out from these notes

- **Coordinated English-source corrections** for roughly twenty-two keys whose
  approved German already reflects the corrected meaning, each with its tests.
- **Two placeholder additions**: `status.fetchFailureDetail` gains `{entry}`,
  fed the localised `routingLog.noResponseExposed`; `status.http.noneDetail`
  gains `{summary}`, fed the localised `status.fetchFailureSummary`. Both
  entries currently freeze the other's English text as a literal quotation,
  which would leave a German screen quoting a sentence it never shows.
- **One new key**, `status.copyReportLanguage`, saying the copied diagnostic
  report is English. It renders only while the interface is German: the report
  stays English in every language, but telling an English reader that an
  English report is in English would be noise. The English entry exists for
  key and shape parity.
- **One missed stage 5 migration**: `RidingWakeLockControl.tsx` hard-codes the
  English wake-lock announcement instead of using `wakeLock.active`. The
  visually-hidden presentation and `role="status"` semantics are preserved.
- **One confirmed production defect**: the control renamed to `Deselect
waypoint` clears the selection but not a pending Move or Insert-after, so
  re-selecting the same waypoint resurrects the old mode. Corrected with
  fail-first evidence, because shipping the new label without the fix would
  make the label untrue.
- **One deliberate non-correction**: `elevation.distanceGuides` pluralises on
  the guide count while its English unit word reads as though it agreed with
  the distance. Correcting the English would mean per-distance unit
  formatting, so the limitation is knowingly accepted as minor and
  non-blocking. German is unaffected — it is written around the guide count
  and `Kilometer` is invariant in the plural.
- **One item allocated out of scope**: the pending-state redesign of the
  48 px Follow control becomes its own numbered backlog item rather than
  expanding item 113.
